model_interpretation.claim: The previous valid OpenMP candidate used a serial cutoff of 512 options per requested worker. Lowering the cutoff to 256 options per effective worker, while limiting the requested team to min(threads, n), tests whether parallelizing medium workloads pays off without creating idle workers or exceeding the passed CPU budget. The controller must measure the cutoff's overhead and any gain; no result is assumed here.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["Factored the per-option formula into an inline helper used by both serial and parallel paths.","Added a static-scheduled OpenMP loop with num_threads(min(threads, n)) so the requested team does not exceed the supplied budget or the number of iterations.","Used a per-effective-worker cutoff of 256 options to retain the serial path for small workloads and contrast the prior candidate's larger work-grain assumption."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Prior OpenMP variants with per-worker grain thresholds have similar aggregate means, but available timings do not establish the serial/parallel crossover by size. This experiment tests a contrasting fixed total-work cutoff: keep the serial path below 2048 options, then request the full passed thread budget (capped by n) with static scheduling. It may avoid region overhead for smaller inputs while improving use of the budget on larger inputs; no gain is assumed.

Instead, cap the static OpenMP team to the number of 256-option work grains available, using the serial path only when that yields fewer than two workers. This tests whether partial use of the passed thread budget can parallelize medium workloads without idle workers, while preserving the existing generic grain and complete output coverage. Prior aggregate OpenMP means are close; no gain is assumed.

items.subject: OpenMP scaling and overhead within the threads budget
items.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare the serial baseline with an OpenMP outer loop using the passed threads value as a hard CPU budget; start with static scheduling and retain a serial path for one thread or small n. Avoid thresholds tied to published test values. Measure available valid n/thread cases under the frozen protocol, verify complete output writes and varied-input correctness, and report overhead as well as any gain. Preserve correct variants for later combination even if they lose in isolation.
